title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Kinesiology and Biomechanics
subject: MTEL

questions.q: Maximum physical strength for both males and females is generally achieved after age 20 because this is typically the time in which:
options: metabolic rate is slowest.
cellular metabolism of free radicals is greatest.
muscular cross-sectional areas are largest.
myelination of the spinal cord is completed.
questions.explain: Muscle force is proportional to its cross-sectional area. Muscle mass and thus cross-sectional area typically peak for both males and females after age 20, leading to the potential for maximum physical strength.

questions.q: In the skeletal system, the function of tendons is to:
options: act as a reservoir for calcium and phosphorous.
attach bones to muscles.
act as the formation centers for cartilage.
attach ligaments to muscle fibers.
questions.explain: Tendons are fibrous connective tissues that connect muscles to bones, enabling movement. In contrast, ligaments connect bones to other bones.

questions.q: Which of the following is an accurate description of the way in which a muscle group generates force during an exercise such as a standing barbell curl?
options: The maximal force-development capacity is limited to the weakest point in the range of motion.
The generation of force remains constant during the entire motion.
The maximal force-development capacity increases as the weight is lifted above waist-level.
The generation of force varies throughout the full range of motion.
questions.explain: When lifting a constant weight, the force a muscle must generate varies throughout the range of motion due to changing leverage and joint angles. Force production is not constant; it peaks and declines at different points in the lift.

questions.q: The tendency of female adolescents to exhibit greater motor control on a balance beam than male adolescents is largely due to females':
options: narrower hips relative to shoulder width.
longer legs relative to total height.
greater body density relative to overall body composition.
lower center of gravity.
questions.explain: A lower center of gravity (COG) increases stability. On average, females have more mass in the hips and lower body, resulting in a lower COG compared to males, which provides a biomechanical advantage for balance.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following principles best describes why individuals with large body builds tend to excel at physical activities that require a great degree of stability?
options: Larger body segments tend to produce more force than smaller body segments.
Muscles with large cross-sectional areas can produce more force than smaller muscles.
A body's inertia, or resistance to change in a state of motion, is proportional to body mass.
A body in equilibrium can be either stationary or moving at a constant speed in a given direction.
questions.explain: Inertia is the resistance to a change in motion. Since inertia is proportional to mass, a person with a larger body mass has greater inertia and is therefore more resistant to being moved, giving them greater stability.

questions.q: An isometric muscle action is characterized by the production of force:
options: as a muscle lengthens due to extension of a joint.
through movement generated in opposition to the downward pull of gravity.
as a muscle shortens due to flexion of a joint.
through tension and muscle contraction without movement.
questions.explain: An **isometric** contraction occurs when a muscle generates force without changing length, and there is no movement at the joint. Examples include pushing against a wall or holding a plank position.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: When a baseball or tennis player swings a bat or racket, the greatest amount of force will be delivered to the ball at impact when:
options: the player avoids stretching the shoulder muscles during the backswing.
the angular velocity of the swinging implement is as fast as possible.
the player reduces the speed of the strike just before impact with the ball.
the linear motion of the swinging implement remains level throughout the strike.
questions.explain: The force delivered to the ball is directly related to the momentum of the bat or racket. Momentum is maximized when angular velocity (the speed of the swing) is at its peak just before and at the moment of impact.
